questions.question: In Case 01, the merchant with fever, what does the modern reading say about removing blood?
options: It is still the best treatment
It does not help; cooling, fluids, and rest do
It works only on the third day
It cures malaria
questions.explanation: Likely a viral or bacterial infection. Cooling, fluids, and rest help. Removing blood does not.

questions.question: In Case 02, the older woman who cannot go, which part of the plan “actually works”?
options: Avoiding all water
Bleeding from the arm
A mustard plaster on the belly
Senna or another cathartic tea
questions.explanation: The plan says senna or another cathartic tea “actually works.” Senna is still in pharmacies, with the same cramping warning.

questions.question: In Case 04, the child who cannot stop coughing, what does Celsus advise?
options: Bleed the child at once
Give a full adult dose of wine
Do not bleed children readily, and do not starve them heroically
Keep her in a cold bath
questions.explanation: Celsus says not to bleed children readily or starve them heroically. The plan uses honey with licorice or hyssop, a warm plaster, and steam.

questions.question: In Case 06, the scaly rash, how do the physician’s and the priest’s jobs differ?
options: The physician names a hot-dry corruption; the priest decides clean or unclean
The priest prescribes herbs; the physician performs rituals
They do exactly the same job
Only the physician may isolate the patient
questions.explanation: A physician may say hot-dry corruption. A priest, if consulted, decides clean or unclean. Those are different jobs.

questions.question: In Case 09, the old man who will not eat, what does the modern reading call “the treasure”?
options: Bleeding for melancholy
The social prescription: food, people, and company
Strong unmixed wine
Complete bed rest in the dark
questions.explanation: Walking with a grandson, music, and refusing to leave him alone. The social prescription was the treasure, not bloodletting.
